items.title: Arnold Loyacano Interview, 1956-09-29
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] such stuff as that. So, uh. There was, did Palomar have another name? No, I don't. Somebody mentioned that, I think the name was The Walking Dance. [INTERVIEWEE] I don't remember that.

ctx.x: played when you were with those youngsters? Oh, well, they, they, uh, those, those days, there wasn't any names to those tunes. They were numbers and, I mean, like number two, that was a tiger rag, you know. And these fellas attached names to them later on. But, uh, they, there's some, some, uh, titles of the tunes were vulgar, too, as you know. Take your hand off a kid's ass. Yeah. And what else? Well, who stole the lock off the shithouse door, you know,
such stuff as that. So, uh. There was, did Palomar have another name? No, I don't. Somebody mentioned that, I think the name was The Walking Dance.

I don't remember that. I don't remember that. What's this, uh, tune that Jack Glenn refers to his prolly? Do you remember that? Oh, yes. Let's see how that went. I forgot now. I forgot just how it. It hasn't been taken and made up into another tune now. No, not that I know of.
